prose_updates.tldr: Separate Brenier structure does not guarantee that a same-unit counterfactual composition preserves Euclidean ranks. The exact population frontiers are unconditional, and the robust open-neighborhood witness provides an unconditional counterexample to the audited Euclidean strict-monotonicity implication. The fixed-support Le Cam lower separation rate is unconditional relative to the endpoint-response program under the stated strict-slack class-constant condition. The reported Hessians remain everywhere defined by clipping at \(m/4\); on the explicitly observed raw-Hessian event with \(r_{H,n}\le m/2\), clipping is inactive and the rank-margin interval and separated decisions are deterministically valid. A class-uniform probability bound for that event, the upper separation rate, and hence the matching two-sided frontier remain conditional on the complete endpoint-response, boundary-wavelet, extension-kernel, nonlinear-remainder, influence-kernel, increment, and concentration program stated in the conditional corollary. For fixed positive tuning constants, the displayed radius tends to zero; therefore, for all sufficiently large \(n_\ast\), a negative margin endpoint on \(\mathcal B_n\) forces the distinct stronger source-product trigger and a terminating validated negative-chord certificate. This event-to-certificate result asserts no probability bound for \(\mathcal B_n\).

project_justification.niche: The delivered field-tier contribution is a graph-native common-rank Brenier counterfactual frontier: exact Euclidean and cyclic structural characterizations, an observable rank margin, an unconditional counterexample to the audited Euclidean strict-monotonicity implication, a deterministic event-to-margin certificate, and a lower testing frontier that is unconditional relative to the endpoint-response program under the stated strict-slack class-constant condition. The class-uniform upper band and matching upper rate are isolated as a conditional program with every analytic and stochastic premise exposed.
project_justification.fill: The symmetric cross-Hessian theorem characterizes Euclidean monotonicity, the commutation theorem characterizes the cyclic-gradient subfamily, and the open-neighborhood matrices separate the full common-rank Brenier class from the stronger commuting subclass and provide an unconditional counterexample to the audited Euclidean strict-monotonicity implication under the displayed dynamic assumptions. The estimator uses a positive density fallback and \(m/4\) spectral clipping on every sample. The event-to-band theorem proves that, whenever \(\max_p\lVert\widetilde H_p-H_p\rVert_\infty\le r_{H,n}\le m/2\), clipping is inactive and all margin and threshold conclusions follow. A separate conditional corollary lists the endpoint-response, boundary-wavelet, extension-kernel, nonlinear-remainder, influence-kernel, increment, and Bernstein-net premises that would yield probability at least \(1-\delta\) and the selected upper rate. The matching-frontier proposition invokes that corollary for its upper inequality, while its fixed-support lower inequality is unconditional relative to the endpoint-response program under the stated strict-slack class-constant condition. Independently of that conditional program, fixed \(C_0>1\) and \(C_1>0\) make \(r_{H,n}\to0\); hence the validated certificate deterministically converts a negative margin endpoint on \(\mathcal B_n\), for all sufficiently large \(n_\ast\), into its distinct stronger source-product trigger and a finite negative population chord.

prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The raw Hessian response is order zero and may accumulate a logarithm, while signed high-order smoothing need not preserve positive definiteness. Spectral clipping at \(m/4\) therefore totalizes the statistic. The proved deterministic theorem makes clipping inactive only on the explicitly defined event \(\mathcal B_n\) when \(r_{H,n}\le m/2\); it does not prove that event's probability. The conditional probability program still needs a uniform boundary-wavelet projection, a bounded polynomial-reproducing extension kernel, the endpoint linearization and quadratic remainder, influence-kernel variance and envelope bounds, an increment bound, and matrix-Bernstein/net concentration. Consequently the matching upper frontier cannot be routed through the deterministic event-to-band theorem alone. The finite certificate is independent of that analytic program but remains conditional on the realized event \(\mathcal B_n\); it uses the source-product allowance \((2M+r_{H,n})r_{H,n}t_{\mathrm{ch}}^2\lVert z\rVert_2^2\), and its trigger is not equivalent to the scalar margin trigger at arbitrary radii. Validated interval arithmetic remains necessary. The lower testing frontier is unconditional relative to the endpoint-response program under the stated strict-slack class-constant condition.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The exact Euclidean and cyclic structural frontiers, the NeurIPS-assumption-aligned open-neighborhood witness, the deterministic event-to-margin theorem, and the eventual deterministic negative-chord implication are proved components. The explicit fixed-support Le Cam lower rate is unconditional relative to the endpoint-response program under the stated strict-slack class-constant condition. The boundary-uniform Hessian endpoint modulus, quantitative quadratic remainder, boundary-wavelet and extension-kernel construction, and influence, increment, and concentration chain are open; none is supplied by the cited sources. Accordingly, class-uniform coverage, the upper separation rate, and a matching two-sided testing frontier are conditional on every premise explicitly listed in \(\mathrm{prop:conditional\text{-}uniform\text{-}margin\text{-}band}\). The certificate itself uses no endpoint-response premise and no probability bound: for fixed \(C_0>1\), \(C_1>0\), and \(\delta\), its displayed radius tends to zero, and on \(\mathcal B_n\) a negative margin endpoint eventually forces its distinct stronger source-product trigger and finite termination. No arbitrary-radius equivalence to the scalar trigger and no termination claim at zero margin is made. No adaptation, irregular-support, coordinate-invariance, unvalidated-numerics, or empirical-violation claim is made. The scalar and simultaneously diagonal cases still reduce to positive derivative ratios.
